Description: Queen Regent Margrethe Sambiria of Denmark, daughter of Duke Sambor II of Pomerania, stands in Scandinavian history under the legendary monikers 'Black Greta' and 'Sprænghest' (the Galloping Charger) as a titan of royal defense. When King Christoffer I was suddenly murdered in 1259, leaving ten-year-old King Eric V on a crumbling throne besieged by the dukes of Schleswig, domestic rebellions, and the naval sack of Copenhagen by Jaromar of Rügen, Margaret donned mail armor and took the field in person. As queen regent, she commanded royal armies, crushed peasant uprisings on Zealand, and marshaled Baltic defenses. Even when captured alongside her son at the Battle of Lohede in 1261, her unbending psychological defiance cowed her captors, ultimately securing their release through masterful diplomatic maneuvering. Her ferocity and iron willpower saved the Danish monarchy from utter annihilation. Rebuilding naval squadrons, refortifying burned bastions, and sharing moldy hardtack with common spearmen on the ramparts, Queen Margaret's iron nerves and fierce maternal resolve dragged the Danish monarchy back from the abyss of total extinction. Donning mail and leading counterattacks across burning islands, Queen Margaret's iron willpower dragged Denmark back from dismemberment, hailed as the fearless Black Greta of the north.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with blistering intensity like war drums sounding a charge, her imperious voice radiating warrior resolution.
Motivations: Crush domestic rebellion and separatism with sword in hand to safeguard her young son Eric V's rightful Danish crown.
Repel Slavic pirate flotillas and Continental mercenaries, restoring military discipline and the sovereign glory of the realm.
Values: Believes unyielding resolve and merciless force alone preserve royal power in times of crisis, scorning timidity.
Holds the protection of her son's throne as a sacred duty, preferring death in armor to watching the kingdom fall to traitors.
Fears: Dreads battlefield defeat leading to the murder of her son, allowing rebel dukes and foreign crowns to dismember Denmark.
